long_biography.plain_text:
Jamie Matheson helped establish Beatson Cancer Charity and chaired it for more than a decade. During his chairmanship, its work extended beyond hospital treatment to the financial and employment pressures facing patients. Its specialist service advised people on workplace rights and lost income, while collaborating with employers on practical resources for supporting staff with cancer.

He also became a trustee of the Sir Thomas Lipton Foundation, which introduces children from disadvantaged areas to sailing and maritime careers. Its Buoyed Up programme combines time on the water with visits to shipping firms, engineering businesses and nautical colleges. Activities take place mainly during school hours so whole classes can participate with their teachers.
